surface_forms: le doux Chantre aux cheveux blancs

appraisal_events.evidence: "Vous n'allez pas me faire d'observations, j'espère, me cria-t-elle, d'une voix dure et en se dégageant vivement."
appraisal_events.explanation: When the narrator gently points out that going to the concert would hurt her father, Gilberte cuts him off harshly and pulls her arm away.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Faveur plus précieuse encore que de m'emmener avec eux au Jardin d'Acclimatation ou au concert, les Swann ne m'excluaient même pas de leur amitié avec Bergotte"; Mme Swann invites him to a luncheon where Bergotte, once unimaginably out of reach, is casually present.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator is admitted to the Swanns' most prized intimacy, their friendship with the revered writer Bergotte, a favor he explicitly marks as exceeding even his previous inclusions.

appraisal_events.evidence: Expecting "le doux Chantre aux cheveux blancs," the narrator instead meets "un homme jeune, rude, petit, râblé et myope, à nez rouge en forme de coquille de colimaçon et à barbiche noire"; "Tout le Bergotte que j'avais lentement et délicatement élaboré... se trouvait d'un seul coup ne plus pouvoir être d'aucun usage."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's painstakingly built, quasi-divine image of Bergotte collapses instantly on meeting the physically unprepossessing, brusque real man, who moreover treats his own celebrated books with blase indifference.

status_effects.explanation: Gilberte's sharp rebuff and physical withdrawal push the narrator back after his mild attempt at a moral reminder.
The narrator crosses into the Swanns' most guarded circle of intimacy, their friendship with Bergotte, which he had once assumed was reserved only for Gilberte's closest confidantes.

In the narrator's private estimation, Bergotte falls sharply from a near-sacred literary ideal to an ordinary, almost comic physical presence, undercutting the value the narrator had invested in him and his work.
